title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from neighbouring pages). Grothendieck works in a 'universal' profinite situation for the 'équation des lacets'. The notation fits the following reading, which is only probable:
- G-hat (𝔊̂) is a profinite completion of a group like SL2(Z) or PSL2(Z).
- ρ and σ are its standard torsion generators. σ has order 4 (L_σ ≅ Z/4Z), and ρ has order 3 or 6.
- Π is a profinite free group of rank two, seen as a subgroup. Π_0 and 𝔊^+ are further subgroups.
- M is a group of automorphisms (or outer automorphisms) of these, with a subgroup M^! and an index-2-type sign character ε_3. Elements τ and τ' are 'orientation-reversing' elements.
- μ = {±1}.
- Π_Q is a Galois-type group, and Π_Q^~ is an extension of it.
- γ_{ρ,σ} is a group built from the pair (ρ,σ). Grothendieck has shown that γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ M(ω) ≅ Π_Q^~.
- N_ρ^* is the set of u ∈ M with u(ρ) = ρ^{±1}, i.e. a normaliser up to inversion. Z_ρ is the corresponding centraliser.

The previous page showed three things:
- N_ρ^{*!} ∩ 𝔊^+ = μ, which is also the kernel of N_ρ^{*!} → γ_{ρ,σ}.
- That map is surjective. The proof splits by the sign ε_3: in one case one corrects u by an inner automorphism α, in the other by α_0 composed with σ.
- The resulting μ-extension of γ_{ρ,σ} is non-trivial.

On this page (614/620), for the corresponding object Z_ρ^{*!}:
- He records the exact sequence (199): 1 → μ → Z_ρ^{*!} → γ_{ρ,σ} → 1. So Z_ρ^{*!} is a μ-extension, isomorphic to the extension γ̃_{ρ,σ}, with γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Π_Q^~.
- Hence there is a canonical homomorphism γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Z_ρ^{*!}/μ → N_ρ^*/μ.
- He notes this is 'of course' the first homomorphism (130) from much earlier. This is a consistency check that two constructions of the same map agree.

Section 9°, 'Récapitulation sur le cas universel'. Grothendieck admits to long detours and to having 'lost himself in the sands', and begins a summary:
- (a)(1): the stabiliser Z_{ρ,σ} of the pair (ρ,σ) is identified with M(0)·L_0^{𝔊} =: M[0]. It acts on 𝔊̂^+ through operations induced by the adjoint (inner) action. M(0) is the part of M fixing the base data, and L_0^{𝔊} is the inner part centralising both ρ and σ.
- (2): inside it, the index-2 subgroup Z^!_{ρ,σ} = M(0)·L_0^{Π} is singled out.

The next page continues the recap. It identifies Grothendieck's diagram of extensions of γ_{ρ,σ} with the extension 1 → 𝔊̂^+ → M → Π_Q^~ → 1, together with its characters χ (cyclotomic) and ε_1, ε_2. In modern terms this is part of his analysis of how a Galois/Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acts on profinite SL2(Z) and its torsion elements, as stabilisers and normalisers of the elliptic generators.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is a bookkeeping step plus the start of a summary, and the claims are consistent with the previous page.
The identification of the map with 'le premier hom (130)' is asserted ('bien entendu') without verification on this page.

ideas.what: Extension 1→μ→Z_ρ^{*!}→γ_{ρ,σ}→1 of a Galois-type group by ±1, obtained from the normaliser/centraliser of a torsion element ρ in profinite SL2-type group under an automorphism group.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of Galois/GT action on profinite SL2(Z) (or PSL2) to stabilisers of elliptic elements; central ±1-extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld (GT), Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (Galois action on profinite modular groups)
ideas.where_published: Related themes are only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche.

ideas.what: Stabiliser of the pair (ρ,σ) is M(0)·L_0, with an index-2 subgroup M(0)·L_0^Π.
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of standard torsion generators in Out/Aut of profinite SL2(Z); orientation sign subgroup

ideas.what: Consistency check that the canonical homomorphism γ_{ρ,σ} → N_ρ^*/μ obtained from this extension agrees with the earlier hom (130).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of two constructions of the same Galois representation into a normaliser

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine consistency step and the opening of a self-summary. The underlying theme (Galois/GT action on profinite SL2(Z) and normalisers of torsion elements) is known from the later GT literature, and nothing here goes beyond that.
transcription_corrections: 'Z_ρ^{α!}' should most likely read Z_ρ^{*!}, matching N_ρ^{*!} on the previous page.
'N_ρ^α/μ' should read N_ρ^*/μ; the previous page has γ_{ρ,σ} → N_ρ^*/±1.
'M(0)' may be M(ω), the notation of the previous page, though the next page also reads M(0); the image is ambiguous.
The struck word before 'groupe' in 'on distingue dedans un sous-groupe' is a deleted, partly illegible word, not necessarily 'groupe'.
